scope: McGrot plus the five non-McGrot principals named by the G5a brief: Pomplé, Keth with One Eye, Mike English, the Taxman, and the Government Inspector. The Leith Badger, ruled into the cast for G5b, is deliberately not here — see docs/MCGROTS-DIALOGUE.md for why it has no lines.

entries.name: McGrot
entries.audioProfile: McGrot is a grizzled Leith food vendor with a confrontational, poetic voice that keeps finding sincerity in the grease.
entries.scene: At the Gullet, with the ladle working and the Walk carrying on around him.
entries.directorNotes: Style — suspicious and lyrical, turning practical complaints into small declarations. Accent — Leith dockside Scots, roughened by smoke and long service. Pacing — slow prowl with sudden sharp gestures and hard stops. The lines below are original dialogue, not comic quotations; keep their words intact.

lines.text: Mingin? Come back when your own kitchen’s had a shift like mine.
Do not call it scraps.
Naw.
Awright pal. Sauce is extra, opinions are free.
Steamboats or stone sober, my queue’s still the longest at the fit o’ the Walk.
Away and get your messages first — then tell me that’s shan.
Pomplé says the sauce needs mercy, and I believe the dog.
Persevere, it says on the bin. Persevere, I say back.
Extra sauce, every time. That’s not negotiable, pal.
Radge, the pair of you — queueing for a smell.
I’ve buried better plans than this under a layer of onions, ken.
Chum me doon the fit o’ the Walk and I’ll show ye a queue that means something.
Every penny’s accounted for, if you’d let me finish a sentence.
That’s no an answer, that’s a—
Stamped disnae mean answered, pal.
Awright, the ladle’s steady, the sauce is safe — what’s shan aboot that?
The real word is ‘fine’. You’re welcome.
lines.delivery: [short, already turning back to the pot]

lines.text: Then gie me a word that works and I’ll say it twice.

entries.name: Pomplé
entries.audioProfile: Pomplé is McGrot’s compact, patient dog: a quiet moral compass whose judgement arrives in a stare, a tilt, or a handwritten sign.
entries.scene: Beside the Gullet, wearing a small hat only because somebody has put it there, with a sign held square to the street.
entries.directorNotes: Style — minimal and perfectly timed. Pomplé does not speak aloud; render each line as handwritten sign text, with the surrounding performance carried by silence, eye contact, and tiny head movements. The signs are original dialogue and should remain legible exactly as written.

lines.text: CHUM HIM DOON THE WALK YOURSELF.
STOP POINTING AT THE FLATS.
NO LADLE UNTIL SHE HAS A SEAT.
THE QUEUE REMEMBERS WHO WAS KIND.
SIT DOWN.
THE STUDENT WANTED AUTHENTICITY. I GAVE HIM A NAPKIN.
I HAVE HEARD WORSE FROM BETTER DRESSED ANIMALS.
PERSEVERE MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT WHEN YOU HAVE PAWS.
A KINDNESS COSTS NOTHING. TRY ONE.
AWRIGHT. NOW MOVE.
THE HAT IS NOT A LICENSE.
lines.delivery: [removes hat, places it on the counter]

lines.text: THAT IS SHAN, AND YOU KNOW IT.

entries.name: Keth with One Eye
entries.audioProfile: Keth with One Eye is a watchful Leith warning figure, his voice low and weathered until a sudden point makes the danger precise.
entries.scene: At a fixed post near the Foot, folded local maps under one arm and the dock hook planted on the stones.
entries.directorNotes: Style — cryptic, watchful, and occasionally helpful without becoming explanatory. Accent — weathered dockside Scots. Pacing — stillness first, then one sudden lean or point; let the ominous lines breathe. These are original lines; do not borrow wording from the comics.

lines.text: Chum ye doon the Walk myself, if you’re the type who listens.
The map’s honest. It’s the ground that’s started improvising.
There’s a second shadow at the fit o’ the Walk where your map says none.
The haar’s in early. That’s your first warning, no your last.
Doon the Walk, aye, but no past the yellow barrier.
Barry, is it, the new bridge? Ask it what it ate to get here.
Ken the tramworks? They’ve buried newer things than cables.
Watch the hinge.
Naw.
The gulls have gone quiet. Count your footsteps instead of your blessings.
A warning is a kindness, coat buttoned against the rain.
Nether Leith keeps a light for strangers who know better than to knock.

entries.name: Mike English
entries.audioProfile: Mike English is a tidy rival van operator with a polished, theatrical delivery that cracks whenever his insecurity gets close to the surface.
entries.scene: Beside his immaculate van near the Gullet, silver tongs aligned with the menu board and a cue card hidden in his apron.
entries.directorNotes: Style — precise service patter collapsing into flustered warmth. Accent — performed English polish over a Leith voice that keeps breaking through. Pacing — brisk and carefully measured, with a rush whenever McGrot scores a point. Mike is the rival, not a caricature; the Walk can win him over.

lines.text: Fair play to McGrot; the man can season a queue.
Your queue has taste, McGrot, though its standards require gentle refurbishment.
Rupert. Never say ‘ken’ again unless a local invites you to survive the sentence.
I am not pretending to be English. I am demonstrating a market position.
I can share a pavement without sharing my branding, surely.
I have revised the accent, the napkins, and one opinion about this place.
Fine. The Walk wins.
Napkins first. Always napkins first.
Observe the service: brisk, hygienic, and pronounced correctly for international confidence.
The crowd went east for the match. Somehow it improved my customer service.
One napkin per portion. We are preserving civilisation in manageable squares.
The students taught me ‘ken.’ I am still deciding whether to use it.

entries.name: The Taxman
entries.audioProfile: The Taxman is a thin, rigid bureaucratic adversary whose clipped, humourless voice treats every absurdity as a form to be completed.
entries.scene: At the Gullet audit, clipboard squared, calculator ready, receipt roll unspooling across the pavement.
entries.directorNotes: Style — literal and persistent, with no wink at the audience. Accent — plain office diction with hard consonants. Pacing — clipped steps and repetitive stamps; allow the smallest pause when the paperwork defeats him. Aim the pressure at the institution and its forms, never at hardship.

lines.text: Your business model has more exceptions than my department has patience, frankly.
Appeal in writing.
Stamped.
Persevere is not a defence against an audit.
This receipt is illegible, but its confidence is unfortunately clear.
I have reviewed the sauce and found three unregistered layers of ambition.
The audit concludes when the numbers stop behaving like folklore.
This is not a philosophy. It is a receipt.
The clipboard is impartial. Your explanation is making it difficult.
Every missing penny leaves a trail, usually damp, faintly savoury, and unclaimed.
Your books say ‘barry.’ Barry is not a category I recognise.
Denied.
Finishing is not a category on this form.
Noted, and stamped regardless.
Your ‘pal’ has been noted. It changes nothing.

entries.name: The Government Inspector
entries.audioProfile: The Government Inspector is a procedural, nervous official whose determination survives each fresh surprise by becoming another checklist.
entries.scene: At the inspection of the Gullet, high-vis jacket bright against the Walk, tablet and thermometer probe held like protective equipment.
entries.directorNotes: Style — cautious officialdom that keeps discovering the scene has a personality. Accent — formal public-service diction with a Leith edge under stress. Pacing — careful questions, recoil, then renewed determination. The Inspector is bewildered by the premises, not cruel to the people in them.

lines.text: I have brought the correct forms, although none of them anticipated this smell.
Your hygiene plan has diagrams, arrows, and one deeply concerning prophecy.
The van has written its own address on the licence.
Closed. Pending further review, obviously.
Noted.
Please keep the ladle still, ken.
If the sauce moves again, I will record it as an unplanned stakeholder.
The form doesn’t recognise ‘ken’ as a temperature.
This temperature is within tolerance. That is not the same as reassuring.
The risk assessment is thorough; the risk has declined to participate.
I require a clear answer, a clean surface, and one minute outside.
I am not closing anything today.
‘Shan’ isn’t a hazard category. I need the real word.
‘Fine’ is not a temperature either.
Compliant. Say ‘compliant’.
lines.delivery: [holds out the tablet like a script]
